gap.description: No top result delivers a candid, first-person 'your first session inside a real open-air Thai camp' narrative aimed at a complete beginner traveler. US gyms cover generic studio first-class mechanics; the Thailand camp sites (NOW, Tiger, Khunsuek) treat 'beginner' as a sales funnel and skip the lived experience: the heat and humidity, twice-daily training rhythm, what a session actually feels like for someone who has never thrown a kick, cultural etiquette (wai khru, mongkol, respecting the ring/coaches), and the family/community vibe vs an intimidating fight-camp stereotype. None has a named, credentialed author (E-E-A-T wide open).

weakness: cultural etiquette (wai khru, mongkol, ring respect) — barely or not mentioned
what a first session genuinely feels and looks like for a zero-experience beginner (sensory, honest, reassuring)
training in tropical heat + practical foreigner logistics (hydration, what to pack, jet lag, single drop-in vs week pass)
no named author / instructor credentials on any guide — zero E-E-A-T depth
fight-camp intimidation barrier not actively dismantled — most copy still leans 'warrior/discipline'
recommended_angle: Position Wildcat's page as the honest, reassuring 'your real first Muay Thai class in Thailand' guide — written/signed by owner-coach Meaw Boonpradub — that walks a zero-experience traveler minute-by-minute through a session in an open-air, family camp: the heat, the wai khru and ring etiquette, what your body will actually do, and why you don't need to be fit or tough to start. Lead with warmth and authenticity (come for the fight, stay for the family) to dismantle the hardcore fight-camp fear no competitor addresses, and own the E-E-A-T gap with a real named Thai author.
